title: lappula rupestris
intro: Lappula rupestris, commonly known as Rock Bells or Prairie Bells, is a perennial plant species belonging to the borage family (Boraginaceae). It is native to the grasslands and rocky outcrops of North America. The plant has been used in traditional medicine to treat various health issues, including its potential anti-inflammatory and antibacterial properties, which may provide relief from respiratory issues, wounds, and skin conditions. The bioactive constituents of Lappula rupestris include alkaloids, flavonoids, and terpenoids, which have been studied for their therapeutic actions, including antioxidant, antiviral, and anti-cancer properties.
